newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods score moderate gains with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods score moderate gains with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot products scored moderate gains with NYMEX by late Thursday, with New York Harbor gasoline differentials firming amid continued short supply and keen buying, players said.
Prompt New York Harbor "M5" winter-grade conventional unleaded sold for three cents over December futures -- about 0.40 cent firmer than Wednesday differentials.
And spot NYH "A5" winter-grade reformulated gasoline was offered at a lofty 3.65 cents over the print, one cent a gallon higher than at the beginning of the week, players said.
Traders said they were still trying to sort out why Tosco Corp unexpectedly stepped up to buy big parcels of "M5" and "A5" grades in NYH on Wednesday afternoon.

Although they initially pegged Tosco's purchases in the 500,000-barrel range, some said the actual volume now seems to have been half of that, with Global Petroleum, Citgo Petroleum and Mobil Corp each picking up 100,000 barrels or more.
There were no indications that the Bayway refinery was having problems, traders said. Tosco declined to comment, citing company policy.
